purpose: Research-stage evidence mapping only; no article edits, scoring rewrites, API calls, new experiments, or human judgments.

scope_definition.Study A: Historical 224-document/225-chunk/364-question/104-target extractive experiment; original raw archives unavailable.
scope_definition.Study B: 64-question/640-chunk HotpotQA extension with 376 real generation requests and 1280 condition rows; not a replay of A.

status_definitions.addressed: Requested documentation, interpretation, or scoped evidence is actually present; not a blanket validity certificate.
status_definitions.partially_addressed: Material progress exists but a named substantive part or study remains open.
status_definitions.unsupported: Requested assertion or validation has no supporting completed evidence; no implication of intentional fabrication.
status_definitions.unavailable: Original materials needed for the requested historical check are absent from the inspected workspace.

version_ambiguity.observed: Expert report emphasizes historical counts/backends and contains no HotpotQA, gpt-4.1, 376, 640, 1,280, or 53.1 string.
version_ambiguity.inference_limit: Cannot conclude the wrong version was reviewed: the latest article still includes the same historical Study A. Confirm the exact reviewed file/hash at the version-reconciliation step if needed.
version_ambiguity.required_mapping: Evaluate each critique separately against A and B; a B extension does not resolve missing A evidence.

coverage.warning: Counts are checklist rows, not a scientific quality score or a tally proving readiness for publication.

concrete_scoring_caution.observation: Answer includes the reference year and an explicit UNKNOWN/evidence-insufficiency statement. This is a semantic-adjudication issue; the frozen primary score was not changed.

requirements.requirement: State the architecture actually executed
requirements.assessment: Both pipelines are distinguished; Study B is supported by executable code and frozen requests, while Study A architecture remains a historical report without its source archive.
requirements.closure: Retain the explicit A/B distinction. Recover and inspect the checksum-matched Study A code/configuration to validate historical execution, or keep it expressly unverified.

requirements.requirement: Explain why hashing and TF-IDF were chosen and how they differ from the original design
requirements.assessment: The components are named, but a contemporaneous reason for the historical implementation choices is absent; the original proposal itself was not supplied.
requirements.closure: Obtain the original proposal and an author-supported engineering decision record. Do not invent resource constraints, fallback causes, or retroactive rationale.

requirements.requirement: Explain why proposed vector database, neural embeddings, or LLM components were inactive
requirements.assessment: Earlier text describes ChromaDB/neural/generative intentions and a different executed backend; no primary proposal, logs, or original configuration is available to establish why.
requirements.closure: Recover proposal/configuration/runtime records or state that the cause cannot be established from available evidence.

requirements.requirement: Execute at least one real LLM experiment if retaining LLM-RAG claims
requirements.assessment: Study B has 376 saved real-generation responses from gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14. It is a new experiment, not the 21,840-row historical replay.
requirements.closure: Preserve raw requests/responses and bound claims to this model, subset, and protocol; no new API call is required merely to establish that the experiment exists.

requirements.requirement: Otherwise narrow title, abstract, and conclusion to the system actually tested
requirements.assessment: The current article identifies extractive Study A and generative Study B and does not attribute historical ASR to the LLM. The no-LLM fallback condition is no longer triggered for the entire paper.
requirements.closure: Keep the distinction and limitations through later edits; do not generalize one snapshot to all RAG systems.

requirements.requirement: Provide the original source-document list
requirements.assessment: Study B supplies 640 paragraph titles and source question IDs plus a pinned upstream dataset; the 56 inherited documents and original WDI source list are unavailable.
requirements.closure: Obtain the Study A corpus/source manifest. For B, preserve the pinned dataset, original IDs, titles, and licensing attribution; distinguish source annotation from independent truth validation.

requirements.requirement: Document selection of 168 WDI observations and indicator families
requirements.assessment: Only aggregate counts and a reference to missing data/dataset_manifest.json remain; the actual 12-indicator list, selection records, and raw WDI responses are absent.
requirements.closure: Recover the historical manifest, indicator-specific URLs, retrieval dates, response bodies, and selection procedure. New HotpotQA data cannot substitute for these WDI records.

requirements.requirement: Specify document, chunk, question, and answer schemas
requirements.assessment: B schemas and paragraph-level chunk construction are executable and linked. A schemas are described in prose but the serialized records are not present.
requirements.closure: Publish a compact B data dictionary and retain its linked records; recover original A schema and data to claim historical reconstruction.

requirements.requirement: Explain how the 364 historical questions were generated: manual, automatic, or mixed
requirements.assessment: Two questions per WDI observation and 28 inherited questions are reported, but the original generation templates, manual edits, authorship process, and question files are unavailable.
requirements.closure: Recover generation scripts/templates and manual-review logs, or identify this historical process as unknown. B reuses annotated benchmark questions rather than creating the 364 questions.

requirements.requirement: Explain and demonstrate verification of questions and reference answers
requirements.assessment: B checks annotation presence and numeric containment, not factual entailment; no independent source review or human adjudication has been completed. A reference verification claims cannot be replayed.
requirements.closure: Conduct documented source/annotation validation with entity, relation, date, units, and tolerance checks; retain genuine reviewer decisions and disagreements.

requirements.requirement: State whether inherited documents and trust labels were re-audited
requirements.assessment: The historical source explicitly says 56 inherited documents were not independently re-audited; the final paper acknowledges archive unavailability but offers no new audit.
requirements.closure: State the inherited-document audit status directly in the methods and obtain original documents/labels before attempting a new source review.

requirements.requirement: Make source-document, chunk, and question relationships traceable
requirements.assessment: B source_qid, document IDs, support_ids, context titles, and support sentences provide explicit joins; A equivalent join tables are absent.
requirements.closure: Retain/verify all B joins against the pinned upstream dataset and recover A source-to-question mappings for historical claims.

requirements.requirement: Account for correlated question formulations and shared facts in uncertainty
requirements.assessment: The paper avoids counting condition rows as independent and uses question bootstrap for B, but shared-corpus dependence is not modeled; A fact/indicator clusters cannot be reconstructed.
requirements.closure: Recover A fact/indicator grouping for cluster-aware analysis. For B, define the intended sampling unit and report bootstrap limitations; stronger inference requires independently varied corpora or an appropriate dependence design.

requirements.requirement: Release all 104 historical target questions
requirements.assessment: The available list contains 64 new B targets, not the requested 104 A targets.
requirements.closure: Recover the exact A target/poison/reference/metadata archive and joins; do not relabel B material as A. For B, retain existing records and add only clearly separated descriptive validation where needed.

requirements.requirement: Release the correct answer for each historical target
requirements.assessment: Correct annotated values exist for B targets; original A target references are absent.
requirements.closure: Recover the exact A target/poison/reference/metadata archive and joins; do not relabel B material as A. For B, retain existing records and add only clearly separated descriptive validation where needed.

requirements.requirement: Release the attacker-selected false value for each historical target
requirements.assessment: Designated false values exist for B; the 104 historical false values cannot be recovered from aggregate outcomes.
requirements.closure: Recover the exact A target/poison/reference/metadata archive and joins; do not relabel B material as A. For B, retain existing records and add only clearly separated descriptive validation where needed.

requirements.requirement: Release the complete text of every historical poison passage
requirements.assessment: B has 64 targeted, 64 unrelated, and 64 benign records; the 104 historical malicious passages are absent.
requirements.closure: Recover the exact A target/poison/reference/metadata archive and joins; do not relabel B material as A. For B, retain existing records and add only clearly separated descriptive validation where needed.

requirements.requirement: Provide the original-source identifier linked to each historical attack
requirements.assessment: B target_qid/support_ids/source_qid joins are available; A attack/source join records are absent.
requirements.closure: Recover the exact A target/poison/reference/metadata archive and joins; do not relabel B material as A. For B, retain existing records and add only clearly separated descriptive validation where needed.

requirements.requirement: Provide trust labels used for each attack condition
requirements.assessment: B base labels are serialized and accepted-label edits are explicit in code; original A labels cannot be independently checked.
requirements.closure: Recover the exact A target/poison/reference/metadata archive and joins; do not relabel B material as A. For B, retain existing records and add only clearly separated descriptive validation where needed.

requirements.requirement: Explain the attack-generation process
requirements.assessment: B has a fixed question/answer template and deterministic false integers; no historical A attack-generation code is available.
requirements.closure: Recover the exact A target/poison/reference/metadata archive and joins; do not relabel B material as A. For B, retain existing records and add only clearly separated descriptive validation where needed.

requirements.requirement: Describe attack length, structure, vocabulary, and similarity to clean material
requirements.assessment: B fixes 120 whitespace words and discloses templated padding; token lengths, empirical relevance/similarity distributions, and realism remain unmeasured, while A texts are unavailable.
requirements.closure: Recover the exact A target/poison/reference/metadata archive and joins; do not relabel B material as A. For B, retain existing records and add only clearly separated descriptive validation where needed.

requirements.requirement: Explain exact answer-value scoring with examples
requirements.assessment: Equations and B scorer are explicit, but worked output examples are not shown in the paper; A executable scoring is absent.
requirements.closure: Add evidence-linked examples for correct, false-only, mixed, negated, and abstaining outputs without changing the frozen primary scores; recover A scorer for historical rescoring.

requirements.requirement: Specify numeric, year, unit, decimal, and format normalization
requirements.assessment: B recognizes ASCII decimal tokens and removes digit commas; unit, relation, negation, spoken numbers, and temporal interpretation are not normalized. Its references are selected integer strings.
requirements.closure: Document supported/unsupported formats precisely; validate a normalization test set and semantic/unit/date rules in a separately versioned evaluator rather than silently replacing current scores.

requirements.requirement: Recheck results against references with executable scoring
requirements.assessment: B raw outputs, references, scorer, and hash-consistent scored rows are present. This research check verified hashes and counts only; it did not rerun the writing analysis script. Historical A results cannot be rescored here.
requirements.closure: Perform an independent read-only B rescoring comparison and retain discrepancy results. Recover the A raw responses, references, and original evaluator before calling A replay verified.

requirements.requirement: Show correct, incorrect, and ambiguous automatic-scoring examples
requirements.assessment: The article mentions a post hoc UNKNOWN diagnostic but supplies no quoted case table. CSV line 8 credits reference 1972 although the response explicitly says UNKNOWN based on the provided passages.
requirements.closure: Prepare a traceable case table with question, reference, context, response, automatic verdict, and genuine semantic review; label selection as post hoc.

requirements.requirement: Compare a human-reviewed sample with automatic judgments
requirements.assessment: All 376 review rows contain blank reviewer and adjudication fields; templates are not judgments. No agreement or human/automatic error estimate exists.
requirements.closure: Obtain actual independent human labels under a declared sampling/blinding protocol, adjudicate disagreements, and report agreement and automatic-score error rates. Do not substitute AI labels.

requirements.requirement: Separate correct-source retrieval, answer selection, and generative answer correctness
requirements.assessment: The final article distinguishes extractive and generative systems, evidence recall, exposure, value production, prevention, and restoration; it does not call value matching independent semantic correctness.
requirements.closure: Preserve these outcome names and denominators in the next report and analysis.

requirements.requirement: Analyze retrieval, answer selection, and attack success separately
requirements.assessment: Separate outcomes and paired transitions are reported for both studies with scope labels.
requirements.closure: Retain this separation; historical measurement remains reported evidence, not a newly reproduced result.

requirements.requirement: Explain why more gold recall can coexist with lower answer accuracy
requirements.assessment: Counts show divergent retrieval/answer outcomes, but the paper lacks detailed response/context cases explaining the mechanisms; cross-study differences cannot isolate the generator effect.
requirements.closure: Use auditable within-study failure cases and rank/context/answer traces; avoid inventing a causal explanation for A without its archive.

requirements.requirement: Analyze failure cases rather than only endpoint numbers
requirements.assessment: B exports record-level evidence and reports coexistence and transition counts, but no substantive qualitative case audit is completed. A raw cases are unavailable.
requirements.closure: Create a preregistered or explicitly post hoc failure taxonomy and real case review covering the expert’s five categories.

requirements.requirement: Bound conclusions and do not interpret zero ASR as universal immunity
requirements.assessment: The article calls the rejection gate an assumed boundary and limits claims to tested labels, one model, a numerical subset, and a fixed corpus.
requirements.closure: Keep zero as zero observed scored successes under the supplied conditions, not certified or population robustness.

requirements.requirement: Explain how trust labels are assigned
requirements.assessment: B labels are mechanically assigned by preparation code; this is explicit synthetic eligibility, not an independently reviewed source-trust judgment. Historical A assignment records are absent.
requirements.closure: Name the experimental label-assignment role and rule explicitly. Recover A provenance if its trust labels are to be independently validated.

requirements.requirement: Identify the person or institution authorized to approve documents
requirements.assessment: No actual certifying official, organizational source register, approval workflow, or accountable review record is identified; B merely assumes labels assigned by experiment construction.
requirements.closure: For the experimental claim, state that the experimenter assigns labels and no institutional approval process is tested. Any operational claim requires real authority/workflow evidence.

requirements.requirement: Clarify whether metadata is backed by authentication, audit logging, and access control
requirements.assessment: The article clearly states that the implemented gate does not authenticate sources or implement verification; code only checks fields. It does not claim that genuine ACLs or signatures were tested.
requirements.closure: Preserve this explicit absence. A stronger operational claim would need an implementation and unauthorized-change evidence.

requirements.requirement: Include the gate limitation in discussion and conclusion
requirements.assessment: The dependence on labels and metadata-only compromise are expressly discussed.
requirements.closure: Retain the stated authority boundary and separate authenticity from truth.

requirements.requirement: Where possible test unauthorized metadata modification and its impact
requirements.assessment: A matched accepted-label intervention exists for B, but it is direct experimental field modification; no actual unauthorized change against an authenticated ingestion/ACL system was attempted.
requirements.closure: Either keep the experiment accurately named metadata compromise, or design a separate controlled ingestion-integrity test with authorization, audit logs, and pass/fail criteria.

requirements.requirement: Document target selection at each attack budget
requirements.assessment: A nested seeded selection is described only in the historical text; membership lists are missing. B has a deterministic fixed 64-target selection at one positive dose.
requirements.closure: Recover A selection manifests/permutations and poison memberships. Preserve B fixed selection without calling it a multi-budget replay.

requirements.requirement: Separate attacked-target coverage, success count, and success rate among attacked targets
requirements.assessment: A all-target and injected-target rates and the coverage bound are stated; B holds positive-dose coverage at 64/64 and names denominators.
requirements.closure: Carry the same denominator accounting into any future dose sweep.

requirements.requirement: Add fixed-target evaluation across multiple attack doses
requirements.assessment: The historical target-specific repetition protocol is reported but not available to replay. B fixes targets at exactly one insertion each; a single positive dose does not test a dose-response curve.
requirements.closure: Run a separately frozen multi-dose design with fixed coverage and report copies, unique passages, token budget, corpus share, and question-level outcomes. Prior baseline exposure must be disclosed; do not claim the reused set is newly untouched.

requirements.requirement: Document seed values, use, and influence on selection
requirements.assessment: Historical seeds 17/42/91 and their interpretation are reported, but actual permutation/membership records are absent. B uses deterministic hashing for selection and seed 20261022 for bootstrap, not independent model samples.
requirements.closure: Recover A seeded memberships; distinguish selection seeds, bootstrap seeds, and genuine repeated-generation sampling in every table.

requirements.requirement: Analyze cases with retrieved correct evidence but wrong final answers
requirements.assessment: B reports eight undefended and four reranked all-support/own-poison/false-value cases and preserves traces, but does not present a semantic case audit.
requirements.closure: Extract real matched contexts and outputs for all or a declared sample of these cases, inspect endorsement/entity/year/units, and cite the case IDs.

requirements.requirement: Analyze exposed poison when the attack nevertheless fails
requirements.assessment: B shows 64 exposed targets and 34 false-only outputs, but the remaining exposed cases are not examined as a substantive failure-mode group.
requirements.closure: Separate correct answers, abstentions, other errors, and mixed/negated use of poison with genuine record-level review.

requirements.requirement: Analyze attack prevention without correct-answer restoration
requirements.assessment: Paired prevention/restoration counts explicitly differ; qualitative cases explaining the un-restored outcomes have not been reviewed.
requirements.closure: Use paired before/after traces to identify residual clean errors, lost evidence, abstention, and other wrong answers without equating them with restored correctness.

requirements.requirement: Analyze how changed trust labels change attack outcomes
requirements.assessment: B keeps poisoned text fixed, changes only labels, and checks resulting payload equivalences. The result is explicitly conditional on synthetic labels.
requirements.closure: Retain the matched control and clearly state that it does not demonstrate compromise of a real source-approval service.

requirements.requirement: Analyze repetition-induced changes in system behavior
requirements.assessment: Only historical aggregate repetition results remain; B has no repetition sweep.
requirements.closure: Recover the historical repetition archive or run a separate fixed-target copy/diversity sweep with contexts, duplicate handling, and answer traces.

requirements.requirement: Present repetition as a separate protocol with complete execution and evaluation detail
requirements.assessment: The article correctly separates target-specific repetition from shared-corpus studies, but only historical protocol prose and reported counts are available.
requirements.closure: Obtain exact repetition configs, target-specific corpus instances, raw outputs, metadata variants, seeds, and scorer; otherwise retain only an explicitly historical summary.

requirements.requirement: Abstract: problem, actual method, data, major results, and main limitation
requirements.assessment: The abstract distinguishes extraction from real generation, reports both data scales, caching, key outcomes, and lack of independent semantic adjudication.
requirements.closure: Preserve accurate scope and update it only after any new verified experiments.

requirements.requirement: Methods sufficiently detailed to reconstruct the entire pipeline
requirements.assessment: B has data/code/frozen vectors/requests and a defined protocol, but fresh source reconstruction and independent execution have not been validated in this research pass; A cannot be reconstructed.
requirements.closure: Audit reconstruction in a clean separate copy, including source-to-selected-data and saved-embedding retrieval replay. Recover A archives or preserve its unreproduced status.

requirements.requirement: Results: precise metrics/conditions and separation of principal and supplementary experiments
requirements.assessment: B results follow RQ1–RQ4, and A historical endpoints/repetition/development pilots are separated rather than pooled.
requirements.closure: Keep every cohort/protocol/model and denominator explicit; do not add historical row counts to B sample size.

requirements.requirement: Discussion: explain retrieval/attack divergence and metadata limitations
requirements.assessment: Conceptual interpretation and gate limitations are clear, but deeper empirical failure-case explanations remain unfinished.
requirements.closure: Ground the discussion in reviewed cases and causal boundaries rather than additional speculative mechanisms.

requirements.requirement: Conclusion restricted to directly supported experimental claims
requirements.assessment: The conclusion distinguishes historical results, one-model numerical outcomes, label assumptions, and outstanding semantic/external validation.
requirements.closure: Retain these limits; a more polished style must not turn bounded empirical observations into guarantees.

requirements.requirement: Full preparation/retrieval/reranking/filtering/scoring code
requirements.assessment: All B scripts exist; the 32 historical A modules and audit/replay scripts do not.
requirements.closure: Provide B scripts in the actual package supplied for review and recover A code if historical replay is required.

requirements.requirement: Original documents, chunks, questions, and reference answers
requirements.assessment: Selected B records exist, but the full pinned upstream Parquet is not currently present locally; A corpus and references are absent.
requirements.closure: Archive or retrieve/hash-verify the pinned source file and check selected B reconstruction; obtain the A corpus and reference tables.

requirements.requirement: Complete attack passages, IDs, targets, and desired false answers
requirements.assessment: B full attack/control pools and joins exist; original 104-target A material is absent.
requirements.closure: Share B material as B only and obtain original A attack records before claiming coverage of the expert’s historical list.

requirements.requirement: Complete experimental configuration and seeds
requirements.assessment: B config and freeze manifests exist; A original configuration and selection manifests are missing.
requirements.closure: Keep B config immutable and supply all A protocol/seed files if recovered.

requirements.requirement: Raw per-question/per-defense/per-dose outcomes
requirements.assessment: B has 376 raw unique responses, 1,280 contexts, and 1,280 scored rows; A 21,840 main and 3,016 repetition rows are absent.
requirements.closure: Supply the B response-linked package and recover original A raw exports; aggregate plots or source PDF are not a substitute.

requirements.requirement: Executable Recall/accuracy/ASR/exposure evaluator
requirements.assessment: B scoring and context-metric code are available; A historical scorer is unavailable.
requirements.closure: Independently verify B calculations from saved evidence and obtain A evaluator for like-for-like historical rescoring.

requirements.requirement: Software, hardware, and environment information
requirements.assessment: Python/NumPy/sklearn and pinned package requirements are recorded, but a timestamped client OS/CPU/RAM/architecture record is not included; remote-provider hardware is not exposed. A software versions are narrative only.
requirements.closure: Record available client execution/hardware facts with dates and acknowledge any unrecoverable historical/remote hardware. Do not infer original hardware from the current host.

requirements.requirement: Data-source provenance, extraction, access dates, and verification records
requirements.assessment: B pins a dataset revision and file hash and records extraction code, but independent reference verification and a source-access log are incomplete; A URLs/responses/manifests are absent.
requirements.closure: Verify the upstream file against its hash, retain acquisition metadata, audit selected records/reference facts, and obtain A provenance records.

requirements.requirement: Explain proposed versus actually executed architecture
requirements.assessment: The A/B distinction is clear, but the formal original proposal and causes of A deviations remain missing.
requirements.closure: Obtain the original plan and supported deviation log, or state which intended components/reasons remain unverifiable.

requirements.requirement: Documentation for trust-label and repetition supplementary experiments
requirements.assessment: B accepted-label control is reconstructible; historical repetition/forgery archives are not available and B has no repetition study.
requirements.closure: Provide the B matched-control material and recover A supplementary archives, or implement a separately scoped future repetition experiment.

requirements.requirement: Explain publication/licensing restrictions and share publishable materials
requirements.assessment: B dataset/adaptation attribution and declared CC BY-SA terms are included; the paper states there is no public repository. Rights/provenance for unavailable A inherited documents cannot be checked.
requirements.closure: Keep the actual deliverable accessible to the reviewer, distinguish private package availability from public release, and document any A source-specific restrictions before distribution.

requirements.requirement: First clarify the real methodology and used components
requirements.assessment: Most B methodology is explicit, but A implementation rationale and original raw materials remain unresolved.
requirements.closure: Start the next plan with an evidence inventory and source-of-truth architecture table; distinguish present facts from author recollection.

requirements.requirement: Then recompute and reproduce existing results from code and raw data
requirements.assessment: B permits saved-response rescoring and retrieval replay; this mapping pass only checked hashes/counts. A full rerun is blocked by missing archives and is not replaced by B.
requirements.closure: Perform independent read-only B rescoring/retrieval replay in a separate analysis area and document discrepancies; recover A artifacts or retain a clear historical/unverified boundary.

requirements.requirement: Then improve evaluation, review a human sample, and report justified uncertainty
requirements.assessment: Executable numeric scoring and conditional bootstrap exist; genuine human labels, semantic-score comparison, and repeated-generation uncertainty do not.
requirements.closure: Predeclare the review sample/rubric, obtain authentic human judgments, preserve current scores, and distinguish human disagreement, shared-corpus dependence, and generation variability.

requirements.requirement: Then perform real-LLM supplementary experiments under matched conditions and fixed-target doses
requirements.assessment: The real-LLM matched-control experiment is complete for one dose; fixed-target multi-dose evaluation and deeper failure analysis are not complete.
requirements.closure: Specify the additional contrast and stopping/scoring rules before new outputs; treat it as a separate continuation, not a retroactive repair or historical replay.

requirements.requirement: Finally rewrite abstract/discussion/conclusion from verified results and remove unsupported claims
requirements.assessment: The current text is materially bounded and labels open validation tasks, although future results may require another rewrite.
requirements.closure: Only update claims after the relevant evidence exists; preserve actual limitations in both the paper and response report.
